All findings identical. ECTS IS THE WHOLE POINT ON THIS ROW: 25 ECTS over 8 months. A 25-ECTS certificate and a 60-ECTS master are DIFFERENT PRODUCTS sold under the same word 'Máster'. Twenty-five credits is roughly 625–750 hours of notional student workload — about five months of full-time study, and well under half a standard one-year master. Consequence for this non-EU candidate, stated plainly: this cannot support a Spanish long-stay student visa on its own. A study authorisation turns on full-time enrolment, and a 25-ECTS programme is not that; only SAE's 60-ECTS, 24-month Máster en Producción de Audio in this same family is of a size that could plausibly qualify. Verify with the consulate before relying on either. THE 300-ECTS QUESTION: the candidate's 300-ECTS Ingeniería Superior degree is exactly what the page requires for the BETTER of the two UDIMA awards — 'un título universitario oficial de Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería Superior o Técnica ... o equivalente' — so he would receive the Máster de Formación Permanente rather than the fallback Máster Profesional. Note this is a Tunisian degree, so 'o equivalente' will require SAE/UDIMA to accept it; get that in writing. No credit-recognition or advanced-standing scheme is published, and 300 ECTS earns no reduction. Minimum age +16 años. Admission is a questionnaire plus an interview with an educational adviser — no audition or portfolio test is mentioned. Content: beatmaking, mixing and mastering in the box, recording, vocal processing and synthesis. SAE is an official Ableton training partner and the programme includes the Ableton Live production certificate.
